actors.notes: Spam-bombing + vishing posing as IT support to obtain Quick Assist remote access [#9 Champion]; downloads and executes malicious scripts via curl/PowerShell [#7]; creates backdoor user for persistence [#4]; heavy abuse of legitimate RMM tools and cloud-hosted payloads [#1 High]. Frequently collaborates with WANDERING SPIDER for Black Basta ransomware deployment. Sub-4-minute attack chains observed.

Callback phishing (lure emails about charges/payments prompt victim to call back) [#9 High]; credential abuse for account access [#4]; stages legitimate exfiltration tools WinSCP/Rclone for data theft and extortion [#1]. Ransom demands up to $8M USD. Long-standing Russia-based eCrime adversary.

Brazil-focused vishing to direct victims to RMM tools (RustDesk, Supremo) [#9 High]; harvests valid credentials [#4 High]; manipulates victim payment systems for fraudulent wire transfers [#1]. Has attempted to recruit insiders at targeted organizations.

Help-desk social engineering to reset MFA/passwords [#9 Champion]; pivots into SSO/SaaS for lateral movement and data theft [#4 Champion]; exploits cloud VM management agents, SaaS apps, and credential managers for collection and downstream targeting [#1]. Sent 700K+ smishing messages via compromised SMS distribution app. AITM phishing for MFA bypass [#5]. Used likely LLM-generated scripts. Diminished operational tempo in 2024 but remains prolific.

GenAI-augmented fake personas to obtain employment under fraudulent identities [#9 High]; abuse of legitimate insider access (Git, SharePoint, OneDrive exfiltration, RMM tool installation) [#1 High]; identity expansion via backdoor admin users in cloud tenants [#4 High]. Deploys BeaverTail/InvisibleFerret via trojanized Node.js coding challenges [#7 High, #3 Medium]. 304 incidents in 2024, ~40% insider threat. Laptop farms identified in IL, NY, TX, FL. Most insiders motivated by salary revenue for DPRK regime.
Big-game-hunting ransomware; often receives initial access from brokers (e.g., CURLY SPIDER), then deploys Black Basta payloads [#7 Champion]. Credential-centric lateral movement [#4 High].

Malvertising via purchased Google/Bing ads (abuse of legitimate ad platforms) [#1]; victims click ads and download from malicious sites [#3 High]; delivers Nitrogen malware [#7 High]. Uses LLM-generated decoy websites to filter non-victim traffic. Filters requests not originating from malicious advertisements.

Exploits internet-facing appliances, particularly Cisco switches [#2 Champion]; chained CVE-2023-20198 (privilege escalation) + CVE-2023-20273 (command injection) against U.S. telecom and professional services entities. Identity pivot post-exploitation [#4]. MitM capability plausible given telecom targeting [#5 Medium] but not explicitly confirmed in reporting.

Exploits web-facing applications for initial access [#2 High]; credential expansion [#4]; uses combination of unique, shared, and publicly available malware tooling for collection/exfiltration [#7]. Likely facilitates intelligence collection operations.

Targets Africa- and Middle East-based government entities, particularly in the diplomatic space [#2]; identity abuse [#4]; business-function misuse [#1]. Previously low-capability adversary that has markedly increased OPSEC posture with anonymization techniques.

Demonstrates extensive knowledge of telecommunications networks [#2 High]; uses compromised telecom infrastructure for routing/relays across regions (MitM/interception capability) [#5]; leverages inter-provider trust relationships as supply-chain pivot points [#10].

Targets technology, gaming, energy, and telecommunications entities in Taiwan and Indonesia, as well as Hong Kong democracy activists [#2 High]; exploits external services, expands identity [#4], deploys tooling for intelligence collection [#7]. Operations likely intended to facilitate intelligence collection.
Credential-centric access and rapid ransomware staging [#4 High, #7 Champion]; observed deploying likely LLM-generated destructive PowerShell script for data destruction on physical hosts.

Develops and maintains Akira ransomware [#7 Champion]. Exploited CVE-2024-3400 on Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN for initial access [#2 High]; RDP with service accounts, credential dumping within 12-14 minutes [#4 High]; privilege escalation via ESX Admins group; uses SharpShares, WinRAR, FileZilla, AnyDesk. One of the fastest adversaries observed. First identified April 2023.

China-nexus adversary targeting South Asian telecommunications providers. Identity-based initial access via VPN, DCSync credential dumping from multiple accounts [#4 High]; deploys LuaPlug and KEYPLUG implants via DLL side-loading [#7 High]. Searched for LAPS attributes and unrestricted delegation objects. Leveraged 11 compromised user accounts in one observed operation. Living-off-the-land techniques.
